name: Crowley Liner & Logistics - Guaynabo (Amelia / FTZ 61)
type: Liner + logistics warehouse / cross-dock distribution center (NVO/LCL, Foreign-Trade Zone 61)

fieldNotes.location: Crowley Liner & Logistics consolidated NVO/LCL + warehouse/distribution at Building #13, Free Trade Zone #61, Carretera 165 (Rd 165) KM 2.4, Guaynabo PR 00965 (Crowley warehouse-relocation announcement). The Edificio-13 address geocodes to the Amelia Industrial Park; CONFIRMED on Street View (pano 18.42414,-66.12042, captured 2023-09) which shows the blue 'CROWLEY' painted wall behind the south fence, and an east-end pano (18.42415,-66.11983) showing CROWLEY-branded red containers + TOTE/blue containers staged on the dock apron. Locked the long E-W gray-roof cross-dock building centered ~18.42462,-66.12080 as the Crowley facility.
fieldNotes.facilityType: This is the liner+logistics WAREHOUSE/cross-dock building, not the marine terminal. Crowley's separate waterfront container/chassis marshalling yard (acres of blue Crowley trailers, ~18.4259,-66.1119, ~1 km NE on the Puerto Nuevo bay) and the Isla Grande ConRo terminal (separate audit, site 06) handle vessel cargo; this Guaynabo building handles NVO/LCL warehouse + distribution.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Single-sided dock bank on the SOUTH face of the building, continuous regular bay rhythm with blue/white/red/orange trailers backed in across the visible center span (z20). Building ~200 m long; estimated ~30-40 total doors -> band 25-50. Door count is an overhead estimate, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Container/trailer staging on the south apron and along the internal service road: CROWLEY, TOTE and blue containers parked nose-in and along the curb (east-end Street View). dropArea 10-25 reflects the on-parcel staging; the much larger Crowley trailer farm is the separate waterfront yard, not counted here.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Fenced chain-link compound with a sliding gate in the south fence off the internal Amelia-park road (off PR-165). Single combined in/out access; no staffed guard booth visible at the compound fence in available panos, so classified remoteGs (badge/kiosk-style access typical of an FTZ building) rather than guardShack -- flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth identified at the Crowley compound gate in 2023-09 Street View; gate is a sliding chain-link gate. Medium confidence.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Paved apron inside the fence between the dock face and the road holds trailers/containers -> internal holding present.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Dense San Juan/Guaynabo metro industrial fabric (Amelia Industrial Park), bordered by the PR-22/PR-165 expressway; clearly Urban.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs in the expressway median south of the park (image), but NO rail spur enters the Crowley parcel.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Single Crowley building/compound within a multi-tenant industrial park; not a campus, so false.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Fenced Crowley parcel only (~200 m x ~90 m) ~= 4.5 acres; excludes neighboring tenants' buildings. Approximate.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Access is from an internal park road with ample stacking room, not directly on a public arterial, so a gate queue would not spill onto a public road.
